CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency Area is Pangandaran Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Pangandaran. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 5. Women are adult humans of female sex and persons recognized by law as Women. 6. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against Women. 7. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capacity, knowledge and skills so that Women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily. 9. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women will or has occurred. 10. Victim is a Woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 11. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the victim. 12. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus, Regional Government apparatus, or individuals. 13. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 14. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or fainting and/or causes death. 15. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person. 16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 17. Domestic Neglect is a person who neglects a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. In addition, neglect also applies to every person who causes economic dependence by means of restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 19. Exploitation is an act that exploits economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others, acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits and/or any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency. 20. Domestic Violence is any act against a Woman that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or Domestic Neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the domestic environment. 21. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a Woman. 22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 23. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by Women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and Women. 24. All Forms of Discrimination Against Women are all forms of discrimination that include territorial dimensions, age dimensions, and special dimensions. 25. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 26.

Article 36

1. The provision of Women's Protection services as referred to in Article 35 consists of Victim identification, legal assistance, medical rehabilitation, psychosocial rehabilitation, Social Reintegration, Repatriation assistance, or other forms.
2. The provision of Women's Protection services as referred to in paragraph (1) is provided for Women Victims of Violence including Victims of Trafficking in Persons, Women in disaster-prone areas, Women workers, elderly Women, Women with disabilities, Women Victims of sexual exploitation, Women heads of households, and other vulnerable groups of Women.

Article 31

The obligations of the family and parents as referred to in Article 25 letter c and letter d shall be in the form of full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women as family members.

Article 40

1. The Regional Government establishes a forum for the protection of women victims of violence at every sub-district level.
2. The forum for the protection of women victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) has the duty to:
a. coordinate and synchronize the handling of protection services for women victims of violence;
b. facilitate and provide more optimal services and reach the lower level community;
c. maintain and develop networks and referral systems; and
d. compile a database regarding the development of protection of women victims of violence.
3. Further provisions regarding the establishment, membership composition, duties, and functions of the Forum for the Protection of Women Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are stipulated by Regent Decree.

ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PANGANDARAN REGENCY

NUMBER YEAR 2019

CONCERNING

EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Basically, Regions are formed to improve public services and realize the welfare of the community, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, regions have obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

The unequal distribution of opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, socio-culture, politics and government, law, education, health, employment and social security, which can give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life is guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to carry out efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and Women to obtain opportunities and rights as human beings so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development. 27. Gender Justice is a process to be fair to men and Women. 28. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the Victim's condition including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that the Victim can carry out their role again properly and naturally both in the family and in society. 29. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence to their area of origin. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims. 32. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and children victims of violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and legal assistance. 33. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports, complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as Repatriation and Social Reintegration for Women Victims of Violence.

Part Ten

Women Victims of Violence

Article 19

1. Implementation of Protection for domestic workers in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, cruel, inhuman treatment, degrading human dignity, and exploitation in employment relations.
2. Domestic workers as referred to in paragraph (1) shall receive protection for:
a. recognition of rights, wages, and decent working conditions;
b. health insurance and social security;
c. access to information and legal consultation services; and
d. opportunity to obtain knowledge and skills to improve economic status.

Article 11

1. Women have the right to obtain health services in order to undergo reproductive life and sexual life that is healthy, safe, and free from coercion and/or violence.
2. Health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. health services during pre-pregnancy, childbirth and after delivery;
b. pregnancy regulation, contraceptive services and sexual health; and
c. reproductive health services.
d. health services implemented through promotional, preventive, curative and rehabilitative approaches.

Article 30

1. The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 25 letter b shall be organized in the form of community participation.
2. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. forming family partners at the sub-district and/or village level;
b. forming women's protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting independent socialization of women's rights;
d. providing first aid to victims; and
e. reporting to the competent authority if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.
4. Provisions regarding forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL

Basically, Regions are formed to improve public services and realize the welfare of the community, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, regions have obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

The unequal distribution of opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, socio-culture, politics and government, law, education, health, employment and social security, which can give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life is guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to carry out efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

The provision of Women's Protection services as referred to in paragraph (1) is provided for Women Victims of Violence including Victims of Trafficking in Persons, Women in disaster-prone areas, Women workers, elderly Women, Women with disabilities, Women Victims of sexual exploitation, Women heads of households, and other vulnerable groups of Women.

Article 31

The obligations of the family and parents as referred to in Article 25 letter c and letter d shall be in the form of full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women as family members.

Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence to their area of origin. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims. 32. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and children victims of violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and legal assistance. 33. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports, complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as Repatriation and Social Reintegration for Women Victims of Violence.

I. GENERAL

Basically, Regions are formed to improve public services and realize the welfare of the community, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, regions have obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

The unequal distribution of opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, socio-culture, politics and government, law, education, health, employment and social security, which can give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life is guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to carry out efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 14. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or fainting and/or causes death. 15. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person. 16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 17. Domestic Neglect is a person who neglects a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. In addition, neglect also applies to every person who causes economic dependence by means of restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 19. Exploitation is an act that exploits economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others, acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits and/or any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency. 20. Domestic Violence is any act against a Woman that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or Domestic Neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the domestic environment. 21. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a Woman. 22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 23. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by Women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and Women. 24. All Forms of Discrimination Against Women are all forms of discrimination that include territorial dimensions, age dimensions, and special dimensions. 25. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 26.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL

Basically, Regions are formed to improve public services and realize the welfare of the community, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, regions have obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

The unequal distribution of opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, socio-culture, politics and government, law, education, health, employment and social security, which can give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life is guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to carry out efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

1. The empowerment and protection of women shall be implemented by integrating gender mainstreaming and gender-disaggregated data in an integrated manner based on laws and regulations.

3. The empowerment and protection of women shall be coordinated by the Agency handling Women's Empowerment.

Article 31

The obligations of the family and parents as referred to in Article 25 letter c and letter d shall be in the form of full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women as family members.

Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and Women to obtain opportunities and rights as human beings so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development. 27. Gender Justice is a process to be fair to men and Women. 28. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the Victim's condition including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that the Victim can carry out their role again properly and naturally both in the family and in society. 29. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence to their area of origin. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims. 32. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and children victims of violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and legal assistance. 33. Basically, Regions are formed to improve public services and realize the welfare of the community, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, regions have obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life is guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to carry out efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Article 30

1. The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 25 letter b shall be organized in the form of community participation.

b. forming women's protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting independent socialization of women's rights;

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency Area is Pangandaran Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Pangandaran. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 5. Women are adult humans of female sex and persons recognized by law as Women. 6. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against Women. 7. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capacity, knowledge and skills so that Women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily. 9. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women will or has occurred. 10. Victim is a Woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 11. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the victim. 12. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus, Regional Government apparatus, or individuals. 13. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 14. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or fainting and/or causes death. 15. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person. 16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 17. Domestic Neglect is a person who neglects a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. In addition, neglect also applies to every person who causes economic dependence by means of restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 19. Exploitation is an act that exploits economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others, acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits and/or any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency. 20. Domestic Violence is any act against a Woman that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or Domestic Neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the domestic environment. 21. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a Woman. 22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 23. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by Women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and Women. 24. All Forms of Discrimination Against Women are all forms of discrimination that include territorial dimensions, age dimensions, and special dimensions. 25. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 26.

CONCERNING

EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Basically, Regions are formed to improve public services and realize the welfare of the community, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, regions have obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

The unequal distribution of opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, socio-culture, politics and government, law, education, health, employment and social security, which can give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life is guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to carry out efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

a. forming family partners at the sub-district and/or village level;
b. forming women's protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting independent socialization of women's rights;
d. providing first aid to victims; and
e. reporting to the competent authority if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.
4. Provisions regarding forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Women are adult humans of female sex and persons recognized by law as Women. 6. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against Women. 7. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus, Regional Government apparatus, or individuals. 13. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 14. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or fainting and/or causes death. 15. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person. 16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 17. Domestic Neglect is a person who neglects a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. In addition, neglect also applies to every person who causes economic dependence by means of restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Exploitation is an act that exploits economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others, acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits and/or any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency. 20. Domestic Violence is any act against a Woman that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or Domestic Neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the domestic environment. 21. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a Woman. 22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 23. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by Women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and Women. 24. All Forms of Discrimination Against Women are all forms of discrimination that include territorial dimensions, age dimensions, and special dimensions. 25. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 26.

I. GENERAL

Basically, Regions are formed to improve public services and realize the welfare of the community, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, regions have obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to carry out efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person. 16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 17. Domestic Neglect is a person who neglects a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. In addition, neglect also applies to every person who causes economic dependence by means of restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 19. Exploitation is an act that exploits economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others, acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits and/or any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency. 20. Domestic Violence is any act against a Woman that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or Domestic Neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the domestic environment. 21. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a Woman. 22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 23. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by Women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and Women. 24. All Forms of Discrimination Against Women are all forms of discrimination that include territorial dimensions, age dimensions, and special dimensions. 25. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 26.

Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and Women to obtain opportunities and rights as human beings so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development. 27. Gender Justice is a process to be fair to men and Women. 28. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the Victim's condition including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that the Victim can carry out their role again properly and naturally both in the family and in society. 29. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence to their area of origin. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims. 32. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the victim. 12. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus, Regional Government apparatus, or individuals. 13. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 14. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or fainting and/or causes death. 15. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person. 16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 17. Domestic Neglect is a person who neglects a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. In addition, neglect also applies to every person who causes economic dependence by means of restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 19. Exploitation is an act that exploits economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others, acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits and/or any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency. 20. Domestic Violence is any act against a Woman that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or Domestic Neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the domestic environment. 21. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a Woman. 22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 23. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by Women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and Women. 24. All Forms of Discrimination Against Women are all forms of discrimination that include territorial dimensions, age dimensions, and special dimensions. 25. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 26.

I. GENERAL

The unequal distribution of opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, socio-culture, politics and government, law, education, health, employment and social security, which can give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life is guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to carry out efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

In addition, neglect also applies to every person who causes economic dependence by means of restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 19. Exploitation is an act that exploits economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others, acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits and/or any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency. 20. Domestic Violence is any act against a Woman that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or Domestic Neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the domestic environment. 21. All Forms of Discrimination Against Women are all forms of discrimination that include territorial dimensions, age dimensions, and special dimensions. 25. I. GENERAL

Basically, Regions are formed to improve public services and realize the welfare of the community, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, regions have obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

The unequal distribution of opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, socio-culture, politics and government, law, education, health, employment and social security, which can give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life is guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to carry out efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PANGANDARAN REGENCY

NUMBER YEAR 2019

CONCERNING

EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Basically, Regions are formed to improve public services and realize the welfare of the community, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, regions have obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

The unequal distribution of opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, socio-culture, politics and government, law, education, health, employment and social security, which can give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life is guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to carry out efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Article 16

1. Implementation of protection for elderly women in order to extend life expectancy so that they can carry out their social functions and play an active role naturally in their social life.
2. Elderly women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall receive the right to Protection for:
a. guarantee of continuity and personal self-development;
b. participation in the fields of education, health, employment, politics, arts and culture as well as utilization of information and communication technology;
c. accessibility of information, legal aid, mobility, social services; and
d. early intervention efforts including treatment and rehabilitation to improve their function and capacity.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 14. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 23. All Forms of Discrimination Against Women are all forms of discrimination that include territorial dimensions, age dimensions, and special dimensions. 25. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 26.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency Area is Pangandaran Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Pangandaran. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 5. Women are adult humans of female sex and persons recognized by law as Women. 6. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against Women. 7. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capacity, knowledge and skills so that Women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily. 9. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women will or has occurred. 10. Victim is a Woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 11. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the victim. 12. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus, Regional Government apparatus, or individuals. 13. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 14. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or fainting and/or causes death. 15. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person. 16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 17. Domestic Neglect is a person who neglects a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. In addition, neglect also applies to every person who causes economic dependence by means of restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 19. Exploitation is an act that exploits economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others, acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits and/or any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency. 20. Domestic Violence is any act against a Woman that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or Domestic Neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the domestic environment. 21. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a Woman. 22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 23. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by Women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and Women. 24. All Forms of Discrimination Against Women are all forms of discrimination that include territorial dimensions, age dimensions, and special dimensions. 25. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 26.

ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PANGANDARAN REGENCY

NUMBER YEAR 2019

CONCERNING

EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Basically, Regions are formed to improve public services and realize the welfare of the community, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, regions have obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

The unequal distribution of opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, socio-culture, politics and government, law, education, health, employment and social security, which can give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life is guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to carry out efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and Women to obtain opportunities and rights as human beings so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development. 27. Gender Justice is a process to be fair to men and Women. 28. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the Victim's condition including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that the Victim can carry out their role again properly and naturally both in the family and in society. 29. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence to their area of origin. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims. 32. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and children victims of violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and legal assistance. 33. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports, complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as Repatriation and Social Reintegration for Women Victims of Violence.

CHAPTER I

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency Area is Pangandaran Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Pangandaran. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 5. Women are adult humans of female sex and persons recognized by law as Women. 6. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against Women. 7. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capacity, knowledge and skills so that Women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily. 9. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women will or has occurred. 10. Victim is a Woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 11. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the victim. 12. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus, Regional Government apparatus, or individuals. 13. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 14. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or fainting and/or causes death. 15. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person. 16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 17. Domestic Neglect is a person who neglects a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. In addition, neglect also applies to every person who causes economic dependence by means of restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 19. Exploitation is an act that exploits economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others, acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits and/or any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency. 20. Domestic Violence is any act against a Woman that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or Domestic Neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the domestic environment. 21. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a Woman. 22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 23. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by Women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and Women. 24. All Forms of Discrimination Against Women are all forms of discrimination that include territorial dimensions, age dimensions, and special dimensions. 25. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 26.

Article 19

1. Implementation of Protection for domestic workers in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, cruel, inhuman treatment, degrading human dignity, and exploitation in employment relations.
